$comment: ★ P68 round 9 (D-CONFIG-NO-SHIPPED-GETOPT-ON-ANY-FORMAT): POSIX puts `getopt` and its four globals (`optarg`, `optind`, `opterr`, `optopt`) in <unistd.h>, and every reference that ships getopt makes them visible there — and ONLY them, never the GNU long API: ✔MEASURED 2026-09-23 by address-of probes, glibc's <unistd.h> (gcc 13.3.0 / clang 18.1.3 default dialect; strict -std=c2x hides all of it) and mingw-w64 13.2.0's (which `#include`s <getopt.h> with `__UNISTD_H_SOURCED__`, so the long half stays hidden) and Darwin's (Apple clang 21.0.0, plus its `optreset` variable). So these five rows re-declare exactly that subset, byte-identical to getopt.json's (the `size_t`/`write` multi-descriptor precedent), and on pe they carry the SAME per-symbol realization as getopt.json — the shipped `runtime/platform/src/getopt.c` — because no Windows image exports them; elf/macho import the platform C library's. `optreset` is Darwin's alone. | Neutral shipped <unistd.h> (POSIX) — c14 (linux) + c15c (macOS). The core POSIX I/O syscalls SQLite's os_unix.c routes through its aSyscall table. The LP64 widths (ssize_t/off_t=i64, size_t=u64) AGREE between Linux and macOS, and SEEK_* + the access() mode bits F_OK/R_OK/W_OK/X_OK are byte-identical (verified against xnu/bsd/sys/unistd.h + _seek_set.h) — so every constant + signature stays flat (no per-format variant). fdatasync + fallocate are LINUX-ONLY (macOS uses fcntl F_FULLFSYNC / F_PREALLOCATE): each carries a per-symbol `availableObjectFormats` of elf-only so it is NOT injected on a macho target (DSS imports EVERY declared shipped extern → a macho-declared fdatasync would plant an undefined import; libSystem has no fdatasync). They ARE injected on elf for linux SQLite's use. (D-SHIPPED-SYMBOL-PER-TARGET-AVAILABILITY) Gated availableObjectFormats:[elf,macho] (elf=WSL run target, macho=macos-latest leg). No over-ship: SQLite's aSyscall surface. open/fcntl/fstat/lstat/stat/mkdir/mmap live in their own headers. c53 += lseek/sysconf/getpid (elf+macho) for os_unix seek/page-size/pid + the _SC_PAGESIZE constant. lseek returns off_t=i64 (NOT i32 — SQLite assigns the result to an i64; a 32-bit return would sign-truncate >2GB file offsets) and ships as PLAIN `lseek` not lseek64 (the default model leaves __USE_FILE_OFFSET64 off, so libc exports the plain name with off_t=8; verified by nm of an -O0 compile). _SC_PAGESIZE DIVERGES per-format (elf=30 / macho=29) so it ships with per-target `variants` (the FILENAME_MAX mechanism); both linux arches share 30 (glibc bits/confname.h is arch-generic). ★ c82 (shell.c CLI): symlink(target,linkpath), isatty(fd), getuid() [uid_t=u32 LP64, the geteuid twin], sleep(seconds)->unslept, usleep(useconds_t=u32) — glibc /usr/include/unistd.h prototypes, identical on Darwin (ride the header [elf,macho] gate). shell.c self-declares `extern int isatty(int);` at file scope — goal-2 lets the user decl win harmlessly (same signature); the descriptor entry serves every other consumer. ★ c85 (shell.c `.cd` command): chdir(path) — glibc prototype verified /usr/include/unistd.h `extern int chdir (const char *__path)`, exported W chdir@GLIBC both arches (nm -D libc.so.6 x86_64+aarch64); identical on Darwin per POSIX (rides the header [elf,macho] gate — the getcwd sibling). C34a (2026-07-21, D-FFI-TCL-DESCRIPTOR test1.c bundle): += _SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN for sqlite src/test1.c:32732 `sysconf(_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN)`. glibc bits/confname.h enumerates _SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN = 84 (elf, both arches — arch-generic like _SC_PAGESIZE). Darwin's value DIVERGES (58) and is not yet witnessed, so this ships as an ELF-ONLY `variants` arm (the _SC_PAGESIZE per-format precedent): a macho target selects no variant -> not injected -> a macho reference fails LOUD rather than folding a guessed value (the fail-loud-over-guess law). TF-C68 (D-FFI-OS-UNIX-LFS-ISNAN-SYMBOLS): += pread64/pwrite64 — the glibc `_LARGEFILE64_SOURCE` 64-bit-offset variants os_unix.c address-takes into aSyscall[] under USE_PREAD64 (Linux-only; macOS/Windows never define it). Signature = plain pread/pwrite (the LP64 off_t is already i64, so off64_t here is i64 too). ELF-ONLY (`availableObjectFormats:[elf]`, the fdatasync/fallocate precedent): macho's libSystem has no pread64, and DSS eager-imports every declared shipped extern, so a macho-declared pread64 would plant an undefined import. glibc exports both WEAK (nm -D libc.so.6: `W pread64@@GLIBC_2.2.5`) — weak = eager-import-safe. ★ D-CSUBSET-DARWIN-BSD-SYMBOL-CLUSTER: fsctl + uuid_t — the Darwin-extensions region of the SDK unistd.h, reached by os_unix.c's plain `#include <unistd.h>` (os_unix.c:94) which THIS descriptor shadows totally, so both names have no source but these rows. fsctl: SDK unistd.h:785 `int fsctl(const char *, unsigned long, void *, unsigned int)` — the path-based fs-control sibling of ioctl that sqlite AFP locking issues at os_unix.c:3013 `err = fsctl(path, afpfsByteRangeLock2FSCTL, &pb, 0)` (the request VALUE side of that call lives in sys/ioctl.json's _IOWR macho arm — the two descriptors meet at exactly this site); libSystem-only export (link-verified; no glibc/msvcrt fsctl exists) → per-symbol [macho]. uuid_t: `typedef unsigned char __darwin_uuid_t[16]` → uuid_t (SDK sys/_types.h:89 + sys/_types/_uuid_t.h:31) — a 16-byte u8 ARRAY, this file's FIRST `typedefs` surface. Typedefs carry NO per-entry availableObjectFormats (a closed key set in shipped_lib_descriptor.cpp) — per-entry availability IS which `variants` exist (the sys/types.json fixpt_t/segsz_t mechanism): the single macho arm matches nothing on elf/pe → not injected → an elf/pe reference stays an honest S0006. Consumers, all inside `#if defined(__APPLE__) && SQLITE_ENABLE_LOCKING_STYLE`: os_unix.c:7600 `extern int gethostuuid(uuid_t id, …)`, :7607 `assert(PROXY_HOSTIDLEN == sizeof(uuid_t))`, :7791 `uuid_t myHostID` — sizeof MUST be 16 (PROXY_HOSTIDLEN) or the proxy conch layout shears. Pinned by tests/ffi RealUnistdJsonFsctlMachoOnly + RealUnistdJsonUuidTMachoOnlyTypedef and the shipped_bsd_random_futimes_uuid_macho corpus, whose exit arithmetic IS sizeof(uuid_t). ★ D-LK-SQLITE-MACHO-UNDEFINED-LIBSYSTEM-SYMBOLS: flock + statfs/fstatfs + sysctl/sysctlbyname — five more Darwin-only libSystem externs sqlite's DEFAULT macho path references (NOT opt-in like the AFP cluster above), each K_SymbolUndefined at link until declared, because DSS imports only DECLARED shipped externs. Consumers: os_unix.c (flock, statfs, fstatfs), mem1.c (sysctlbyname), test1.c (sysctl). PLACEMENT is organizational, not functional — the consuming oracle is a global scan of symbols[].name across ALL descriptors, so it does not matter which file a row lives in; they join fsctl HERE (rather than in new sys/file.json + sys/mount.json + sys/sysctl.json descriptors) because a descriptor SHADOWS the real SDK header TOTALLY (src/core/types/include_path_resolve.hpp:75-79), so a new partial descriptor would REGRESS the D-INCLUDE-ANGLE-SOURCE-FALLBACK that currently makes these TUs compile — the exact reason fsctl, a <sys/mount.h> name, already lives in this file. Signatures MEASURED against the real SDK (xcrun --show-sdk-path), each compile-verified by assigning the SDK symbol to a function pointer of the declared shape under `-Werror -Wincompatible-pointer-types`: flock = sys/fcntl.h:616 `int flock(int, int)` — NOTE it is NOT in sys/file.h, whose __BEGIN_DECLS block is EMPTY and which merely re-includes sys/fcntl.h; statfs = sys/mount.h:460 `int statfs(const char *, struct statfs *)`; fstatfs = sys/mount.h:442 `int fstatfs(int, struct statfs *)`; sysctl = sys/sysctl.h:800 `int sysctl(int *, u_int, void *, size_t *, void *, size_t)`; sysctlbyname = sys/sysctl.h:802 `int sysctlbyname(const char *, void *, size_t *, void *, size_t)`. `struct statfs *` becomes ptr<void> (the fsctl/futimes opaque-pointer convention — no consumer here needs its layout); size_t* becomes ptr<u64> and u_int becomes u32 (sys/_types/_u_int.h:30 `typedef unsigned int u_int`, _Static_assert-verified 4 bytes unsigned). All five carry FLAT signatures with no data-model arm, and that flatness is CORRECT rather than lazy: each row is [macho]-gated and all EIGHT macho64-* formats declare dataModel LP64, so no other data model can ever select them (the random/strtoll availability-narrowed rationale). ★★ TF-C121 (D-FFI-SHIPPED-SYMBOL-PER-TARGET-LINK-NAME) — statfs/fstatfs now carry the per-arch link name, and the CAVEAT that used to stand here CLOSED WITH A FALSE REASSURANCE that must be recorded, not quietly deleted. It said: 'on an x86_64-macho host the SDK asm label makes the call site reference `_statfs$INODE64` while this row imports `_statfs`, i.e. the leg stays LOUD (K_SymbolUndefined) rather than silently misbinding.' ⛔ MEASURED FALSE, and wrong in the dangerous direction. A DESCRIPTOR SHADOWS THE SDK HEADER TOTALLY — src/core/types/include_path_resolve.hpp states the `#include <h>` precedence as '1. Descriptor … 2. Source — NO descriptor, but a REAL source header on the -I includeDirs', so once unistd.json exists the SDK's `__DARWIN_INODE64` asm label NEVER PARTICIPATES in the build at all. There is no call site left to reference `_statfs$INODE64`: DSS declares the plain name, DSS imports the plain name, libSystem's x86_64 slice EXPORTS the plain name (the legacy 32-bit-ino_t implementation), so the program links clean, loads clean, and misbinds SILENTLY. The whole 'the header disagrees with us so the linker will catch it' reasoning presumed a header we had already replaced. The same wrong inference sat in sys/stat.json and dirent.json; all three are corrected. ★ The measurement is unchanged and still holds (sys/cdefs.h `__DARWIN_ONLY_64_BIT_INO_T` = 0 on x86_64 / 1 on arm64; matched two-arch control on macOS 26.5.2 emits `_statfs$INODE64`/`_fstatfs$INODE64` vs `_statfs`/`_fstatfs`) — only the CONSEQUENCE was misjudged. The fix is the exact structural analogue of what `version` did for elf, as predicted: `linkName` declares the UNDECORATED base per (arch, format) and the ENGINE composes Mach-O's leading `_`. ★ AND THE AUTHORING CHECKLIST MISSED IT TOO: 'verify the symbol is exported' passes here, because BOTH spellings are exported by libsystem_kernel.tbd. The check that works is 'does a real compiler for THIS target emit THIS name for THIS C identifier'. ★ `environ` (P68 round 11, D-FFI-ENVIRON-NOT-SHIPPED) — POSIX's name for the environment (XBD 8.1: the array is pointed to by the external variable environ), and POSIX gives it ONE spelling: the PROGRAM's own `extern char **environ;`. No POSIX header declares it (POSIX.1-2024's <unistd.h> declares optarg, opterr, optind and optopt, and nothing else), glibc's <unistd.h> does only under `_GNU_SOURCE`, Apple's never. ✔MEASURED 2026-09-24: that program-declared spelling builds and runs (exit 42, agreeing with setenv/getenv) under gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 (x86_64), aarch64-linux-gnu-gcc 13.3.0, mingw-w64 13.2.0, MSVC 14.51 and Apple clang 21.0.0 (arm64 and x86_64), and DSS REFUSED it on every pair (K_SymbolUndefined `environ`; `_environ` on Mach-O), because no descriptor realized the NAME. ★★ SO `environ` IS A DATA-OBJECT ROW HERE, on elf AND macho: glibc exports `environ`, `_environ` and `__environ` as ONE object at ONE address (0x20ad58 @GLIBC_2.2.5 x86_64 / 0x1b7288 @GLIBC_2.17 aarch64, `nm -D` and `objdump -T` concurring; `environ` is WEAK, and weak is safe: present ⇒ resolvable at load, only ABSENT breaks), libSystem exports `_environ`, and every ELF and Mach-O format binds data imports GOT-INDIRECT — the image DEFINES NOTHING — so a program's own declaration, in a TU with or without <unistd.h>, binds the platform's one object (MEASURED: DSS's Mach-O images carry a `__got` bind of `_environ` from libSystem). `__environ` stays an elf row: glibc declares it unconditionally. pe is realized in stdlib.json instead, as the macro both Windows references ship (`environ` -> `_environ` -> the UCRT accessor), because no Windows CRT exports a bare `environ` (ucrtbase exports no spelling at all; msvcrt only the underscored `_environ`, ordinal 270). ⓘ HISTORY, KEPT BECAUSE IT EXPLAINS THE SHAPE THAT WENT: the first cut of this row was an `environ` object bound by COPY RELOCATION, and it READ NULL on all four legs — a copy relocation redirects libc's references only for the name the exec claims, and glibc's startup writes `__environ` (root-caused by a matched `gcc -no-pie` control whose copy relocation is against `__environ`) — so it became an elf macro `environ` -> `__environ`. Copy relocation is DELETED (D-LK-ELF-COPY-RELOC-CLAIMS-ONE-NAME-OF-AN-ALIAS-SET); under got-indirect every spelling resolves to the one object, and the macro had become the defect: it acted only in a TU that includes <unistd.h>, so the POSIX spelling never bound, and it silently renamed every `environ` identifier of a TU that does. ⚠ THE `@@GLIBC_x.y` SUFFIX MEANS A GREP ANCHORED ON `$` RETURNS A FALSE ABSENT — the stdio.json popen/pclose warning, and the reason the matcher here is ` (environ|_environ|__environ)(@|$)`. ⓘ DSS's <unistd.h> declares `environ` on elf and macho unconditionally, as glibc's does under `_GNU_SOURCE`: this directory models no feature-test macros, its headers are the platform's superset. WITNESS: examples/c/environ_declared_by_the_program (every pair, with a `release` arm), examples/c/shipped_environ and examples/c/environ_alias_object_identity (elf), tests/ffi test_environ_data_object_binding (exactly one realization per format). ★★★ LANE-CFG: `<unistd.h>` OPENS ON pe, MODELLED ON WHAT THE REFERENCE HEADER ACTUALLY IS — A THIN RE-EXPORT. ✔MEASURED against the same-platform oracle `C:/Strawberry/c/bin/x86_64-w64-mingw32-gcc` (`-dumpmachine` = x86_64-w64-mingw32), whose `<unistd.h>` #includes <io.h>, <process.h>, <getopt.h> and then declares ONLY sleep/usleep/ftruncate/ftruncate64/truncate/truncate64/swab/getpid itself plus SEEK_* and STD{IN,OUT,ERR}_FILENO. Per-header probe (one TU each, `void *p = (void*)&NAME;`, rc read directly): <io.h> alone yields close read write lseek unlink rmdir access getcwd chdir isatty dup dup2; <process.h> alone yields getpid; <getopt.h> yields none of them. So the pe surface here is TWO gated `includes` edges (io.h, process.h) plus this file's own CONSTANTS — and NOT ONE symbol row is added on pe, which is why there is no `library.pe` key: on pe this descriptor imports nothing. Every previously-FLAT symbol row therefore carries an explicit `availableObjectFormats:[elf,macho]`; without it the header opening on pe would have declared 26 POSIX externs against a runtime that exports NONE of them, breaking every pe binary's LOAD at 0xC0000139 ([[D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT]]). ★ THE NAMES THE EDGES CARRY ARE DECLARED WHERE MINGW DECLARES THEM (io.json / process.json), as real FUNCTIONS with a per-format `linkName` onto the underscored ucrtbase export — NOT as macros: mingw declares `int write(int,const void*,unsigned)` and links it to `_write` through oldnames, and a `#define write _write` would additionally rewrite every struct member and local of that name. ★ DELIBERATELY ABSENT ON pe, each with its reason: getopt/optarg/optind/opterr/optopt — there is NO getopt.json in the corpus and an `includes` edge to a descriptor that does not exist is refused (invariant: EDGE FIRES ⇒ CHILD AVAILABLE); sleep/usleep — ucrtbase exports NEITHER, and the `_sleep` it DOES export takes MILLISECONDS where POSIX `sleep` takes SECONDS, so a linkName onto it would be a silent 1000x error of exactly the class this project refuses (the honest realization is a shipped-source body over kernel32 `Sleep`, and no consumer asks for one); ftruncate/ftruncate64/truncate/truncate64 — mingw realizes ftruncate as a header INLINE over `_chsize`, so no export named ftruncate exists to bind and the authoring check ('does a real compiler for THIS target emit THIS name for THIS C identifier') fails for a `_chsize` linkName; swab — `_swab` is a real ucrtbase export and the ABI matches byte for byte, but DSS declares `swab` on NO format today, so a pe-only arm would be the only place it exists. ★ THE CONSTANTS BELOW ARE FLAT AND THAT IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED: mingw's <io.h> defines F_OK 0 / X_OK 1 / W_OK 2 / R_OK 4 — byte-identical to the xnu/glibc values already recorded above — and SEEK_SET/CUR/END 0/1/2 come from mingw's <unistd.h> itself. STD{IN,OUT,ERR}_FILENO 0/1/2 are NEW and close a gap on EVERY format, not just pe: glibc /usr/include/unistd.h:210-212 and mingw <unistd.h>:22-25 both define them and DSS declared them nowhere. ★★ THE NON-SYMBOL SURFACES WERE CENSUSED TOO, AND THE ANSWER IS 'ALREADY GATED' — RECORDED WITH ITS MEASUREMENT SO IT IS NOT RE-LITIGATED. Opening a header on a new format is a per-ROW question on EVERY surface kind, not just `symbols`, and the four non-symbol rows here that mingw does NOT provide (`environ` macro, `uuid_t` typedef, `_SC_PAGESIZE` and `_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN` constants — each probed against the oracle with a `#include <unistd.h>` TU; ⓘ P68 round 11: `environ` is no longer a macro here but a data-object row gated [elf, macho] — per-symbol availability, the same effect on pe, RE-MEASURED 2026-09-24: `#include <unistd.h>` alone leaves `environ` undeclared on pe64 under DSS as under mingw-w64's own <unistd.h>, and pe's `environ` is <stdlib.h>'s, where both Windows references put it) needed no edit, because for `macros`/`typedefs`/`constants` PER-ENTRY AVAILABILITY *IS* WHICH `variants` EXIST (the sys/types.json fixpt_t/segsz_t mechanism, already stated above) and all four are variants-only with no pe arm. ✔MEASURED THROUGH THE COMPILER, not read off the JSON, and with a DISCRIMINATING control so the result cannot be vacuous: one TU per name, `--target` the only difference — `environ`, `_SC_PAGESIZE`, `_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN` are RESOLVED on elf64 and FAIL LOUD on pe64; `uuid_t` fails loud on both (its only arm is macho); and the seven rows that MUST survive on pe (`SEEK_SET/CUR/END`, `F_OK/X_OK/W_OK/R_OK`, `STD{IN,OUT,ERR}_FILENO`) RESOLVE on both. A gate that never fires and a gate that fires on everything look identical without that second half. ★ THE GENERAL RULE THE `_SC_*` PAIR ILLUSTRATES: AN ARGUMENT CONSTANT TRAVELS WITH ITS FUNCTION. `_SC_PAGESIZE` and `_SC_NPROCESSORS_ONLN` exist only to be passed to `sysconf`, and `sysconf` is `[elf,macho]` — so a pe arm on either constant would publish a value whose ONLY consumer is a name that fails loud on that target, i.e. a surface that can be spelled and can never be used. Whenever a constant's meaning is 'the argument selecting a behaviour of F', its availability set must be a SUBSET of F's; the two are one fact and drifting them apart produces a header that lies in the quiet direction. ★★★ OPERATOR RULING ("if we need to build some of our own headers, SO BE IT. DO IT. NO WORKAROUNDS"): the names mingw's <unistd.h> declares ITSELF now SHIP ON pe AS A REALIZED BODY, `runtime/platform/src/unistd.c` (the dirent.c precedent; `realization.pe` is the binding fact and there is deliberately no `library.pe`, since one format naming both an image and a source is refusal R3). 'No consumer asks for it' was REJECTED as a reason to omit a name the reference declares — the bar is bidirectional. THE SEVEN: sleep, usleep, ftruncate, ftruncate64, truncate, truncate64, swab. ★★ EACH IS A BODY RATHER THAN A `linkName` FOR A MEASURED REASON, AND THE FIRST IS A TRAP: ucrtbase DOES export `_sleep`, and it takes MILLISECONDS where POSIX `sleep` takes SECONDS, so binding it would link clean, load clean and sleep 1/1000th of the request — `objdump -p` over 4340 name-table entries finds `_sleep` and finds NO `sleep`/`usleep` at all. `ftruncate` is a HEADER INLINE over `_chsize` on mingw, so no symbol of that name exists to bind and the linkName authoring check fails by construction. ⓘ WIDTHS: `off32_t` is `long`, which LLP64 makes 32-bit, so the un-suffixed pair carries an i32 offset and the `64` pair i64 — collapsing them would silently truncate every offset above 2 GiB, which is the whole reason both spellings exist. ★ `swab` ALSO LANDS ON elf/macho, because glibc declares it (/usr/include/unistd.h:1171 `void swab(const void*, void*, ssize_t)`, exported `T swab@@GLIBC_2.2.5` — STRONG, eager-import safe) and DSS declared it on no format: the pe row carries mingw's `(char*,char*,int)` shape and the POSIX row glibc's, hence two rows rather than one. ★★ RED-ON-DISABLE, RUN AGAINST THE REAL BODY AND REPORTED PER MUTANT: sleep-as-milliseconds -> exit 4 with the witness's WALL TIME collapsing 1306ms -> 289ms (the exact `_sleep` signature); swab-without-swapping -> exit 16384; ftruncate-returns-0-without-resizing -> exit 256. Each mutant differed by md5, still parsed, reddened ONLY its own bit, and the RESTORED column returned to exit 0 at 1293ms. ★ F_OK/X_OK/W_OK/R_OK MOVED TO PER-FORMAT arms here (elf+macho) because mingw defines them in <io.h>:182-185, not in <unistd.h> — on pe they now arrive over the io.h edge, which is both reference-true AND why no duplicate name enters the pe closure.
